title: Linkiir Scripting API
description: Reference for the Lua scripting API available inside Linkiir workflow scripts.

modules.name: script.globals
modules.title: Script Globals
modules.description: Values and functions available in every script without requiring any module: the script's input payload, the current node directory, and stdlib-style helpers for loading modules and debug printing.

items.name: Data
items.description: The inbound message/request payload passed to `main(Data)`. For Source HTTP nodes this is the raw HTTP request text; for Transform/LLP nodes it is the message body.

examples.code:
local Raw = Data
print(#Raw)

items.name: __node_dir
items.summary: Deprecated. Filesystem path to the current node directory - use linkiir.sys.nodeDir().
items.description: Deprecated: use linkiir.sys.nodeDir() instead. Filesystem path to the current node directory, set by the runtime before script execution. Still populated and not scheduled for removal, but linkiir.sys.nodeDir() is the documented form. Concatenating it onto a schema name is no longer needed either - a relative schema path already resolves against the node directory.

returns.name: string
returns.description: absolute path to the node directory.

examples.code:
-- Deprecated form:
local SchemaPath = __node_dir .. '/demo.json'

-- Current form - relative schema paths resolve against the node directory:
local Msg = linkiir.data.extract{ schema = 'demo.json', data = Data }

items.name: require
items.description: Loads a Lua module. Search path: node dir (including any linked library dependencies, staged there at run time), then the project's common/ dir (shared modules), then system defaults.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error when the module cannot be found.

examples.code:
local Adapter = require('legacy_adapter')
Adapter.transform(Data)

items.name: print
items.description: Prints values to stdout, prefixed with the node ID.

examples.code: print('processing', linkiir.sys.guid(128))

items.name: trace
items.description: Pretty-prints values to stdout (legacy debug trace). Recursively expands tables.

examples.code: trace({ id = 1, items = { 'a', 'b' } })

items.name: type
items.description: Returns the type of its only argument, coded as a string: "nil", "boolean", "number", "string", "table", "function", "thread", or "userdata".

examples.code:
print(type(Data))     -- "string"
print(type(nil))      -- "nil"
print(type({}))       -- "table"

items.name: tostring
items.summary: Convert a value to a printable string.
items.description: Receives a value of any type and converts it to a string in a reasonable format.

examples.code:
print(tostring(42))     -- "42"
print(tostring(nil))    -- "nil"

items.name: tonumber
items.summary: Convert a value to a number.
items.description: Tries to convert its argument to a number. If the argument is already a number or a string convertible to a number, returns that number; otherwise returns nil. An optional base (2-36) interprets e as an integer in that base.

returns.description: number, or nil if the conversion fails

examples.code:
print(tonumber('42'))      -- 42
print(tonumber('2A', 16)) -- 42
print(tonumber('abc'))    -- nil

items.name: pairs
items.usage: for k, v in pairs(t) do ... end
items.summary: Iterate all key/value pairs of a table.
items.description: Returns three values (next, t, nil) so that a generic for loop iterates over all key/value pairs of table t, in an undefined order.

returns.description: next, t, nil (for use in a generic for loop)

examples.code:
local Headers = { ['Content-Type'] = 'text/plain', ['X-Id'] = '123' }
for k, v in pairs(Headers) do
   print(k, v)
end

items.name: ipairs
items.usage: for i, v in ipairs(t) do ... end
items.summary: Iterate the array part of a table in order.
items.description: Returns three values so that a generic for loop iterates over the pairs (1, t[1]), (2, t[2]), ..., up to the first nil value.

returns.description: iterator function, t, 0 (for use in a generic for loop)

examples.code:
local Files = linkiir.sys.fs.list{ path = '/inbound' }
for i, f in ipairs(Files) do
   print(i, f)
end

items.name: next
items.description: Returns the next key/value pair after key k in table t, in an undefined order; returns nil when there are no more. Called with k = nil (or omitted) returns the first pair. Underlies pairs().

params.name: k
params.description: Previous key; omit to get the first pair.

returns.description: nextKey, nextValue, or nil when exhausted

examples.code:
local k, v = next(Headers)
while k do
   print(k, v)
   k, v = next(Headers, k)
end

items.name: select
items.summary: Count or pick from a variadic argument list.
items.description: If index is the string "#", returns the total number of extra arguments. Otherwise returns all arguments from index onward.

returns.description: the selected arguments, or a count when index is "#"

examples.code:
local function Count(...)
   return select('#', ...)
end
print(Count('a', 'b', 'c'))  -- 3
print(select(2, 'a', 'b', 'c'))  -- "b"  "c"

items.name: error
items.description: Terminates the last protected function called (or the whole script) and returns message as the error object. level controls where position info is added (1 = the caller of error, the default).

examples.code: if not Resp then error('request failed') end

items.name: assert
items.summary: Raise an error if v is falsy.
items.description: If v is false or nil, calls error(message), using "assertion failed!" as a default message. Otherwise returns all its arguments.

params.name: message
params.description: Error value used when v is falsy.

returns.description: v, ... (all arguments, unchanged, when v is truthy)

examples.code: local Mrn = assert(Msg.PID[3][1][1]:value(), 'missing MRN')

items.name: pcall
items.summary: Call a function in protected mode.
items.description: Calls f with the given arguments in protected mode: any error inside f is caught instead of propagating. Returns true plus f's results on success, or false plus the error object on failure.

examples.code:
local Ok, Msg, MsgType = pcall(linkiir.data.extract, { schema = 'demo.json', data = Data })
if not Ok then error('extract failed: ' .. tostring(Msg)) end

items.name: xpcall
items.summary: Call a function in protected mode with a message handler.
items.description: Like pcall, but calls the message handler msgh in the context of the error, before the stack unwinds — useful for attaching a traceback.

params.name: msgh
params.description: Message handler, called with the error object.

examples.code:
local Ok, Err = xpcall(function() return riskyStep() end, debug.traceback)
if not Ok then print(Err) end

items.name: unpack
items.summary: Expand a table into multiple return values.
items.description: Returns the elements from the given table list, from list[i] to list[j]. Defaults are i = 1 and j = #list.

examples.code:
local Args = { 'a', 'b', 'c' }
print(unpack(Args))  -- "a"  "b"  "c"

items.name: rawequal
items.description: Checks whether v1 is equal to v2, without invoking the __eq metamethod.

examples.code: print(rawequal(1, 1))  -- true

items.name: rawget
items.summary: Read a table field without metamethods.
items.description: Gets the real value of t[k], without invoking the __index metamethod.

examples.code: print(rawget(SomeTable, 'id'))

items.name: rawset
items.summary: Write a table field without metamethods.
items.description: Sets the real value of t[k] to v, without invoking the __newindex metamethod. Returns t.

examples.code: rawset(SomeTable, 'id', 42)

items.name: setmetatable
items.summary: Attach a metatable to a table.
items.description: Sets the metatable for table t. Returns t.

params.name: metatable
params.description: New metatable, or nil to remove it.

examples.code: local Vector = setmetatable({ x = 1, y = 2 }, VectorMeta)

items.name: getmetatable
items.description: Returns the metatable of t, or nil if it has none (or the metatable's __metatable field, if that is set).

examples.code: local Meta = getmetatable(Vector)

items.name: collectgarbage
items.description: Runs garbage-collector actions. With no arguments, performs a full collection cycle. opt selects the action (e.g. "collect", "count", "step").

returns.description: depends on opt (e.g. current memory use in Kbytes for "count")

examples.code:
collectgarbage()               -- full collection cycle
print(collectgarbage('count'))  -- current memory use, in Kbytes

items.name: _VERSION
items.description: A global variable (not a function) holding a string with the running Lua version, e.g. "Lua 5.1".

examples.code: print(_VERSION)  -- "Lua 5.1"

items.name: _G
items.description: The table representing the script's global environment. Reading/writing _G.x is equivalent to reading/writing the global variable x.

examples.code:
_G.Counter = 0
print(Counter)  -- 0

items.name: dofile
items.summary: Execute a Lua file as a chunk.
items.description: Loads and immediately runs the Lua chunk in filename (or stdin, if omitted), in the global environment. Errors propagate to the caller, unprotected. Prefer require for loading reusable modules — dofile re-runs the file every call and has no module caching.

params.name: filename
params.description: Path of the Lua file to run. Default stdin.

examples.code: dofile(linkiir.sys.nodeDir() .. '/helpers.lua')

items.name: loadfile
items.summary: Load a Lua file without running it.
items.description: Loads a chunk from filename (or stdin, if omitted) without running it. Returns the compiled chunk as a function, or nil plus an error message on a syntax error.

params.name: filename
params.description: Path of the Lua file to load. Default stdin.

returns.description: function on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local Chunk, Err = loadfile(linkiir.sys.nodeDir() .. '/helpers.lua')
if Chunk then Chunk() end

items.name: loadstring
items.summary: Compile a Lua chunk from a string.
items.description: Loads a chunk from the given string without running it. Returns the compiled chunk as a function, or nil plus an error message on a syntax error. chunkname is used in error messages and debug info.

params.name: chunkname
params.description: Name used in error messages/tracebacks. Default the string itself.

returns.description: function on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local Chunk = loadstring('return 1 + 1')
print(Chunk())  -- 2

items.name: load
items.summary: Compile a Lua chunk from a reader function.
items.description: Loads a chunk using func, a reader function repeatedly called with no arguments that must return successive pieces of the chunk's source (or nil/empty string to signal the end). Returns the compiled chunk as a function, or nil plus an error message on a syntax error.

params.name: func
params.description: Reader function returning successive source chunks.

returns.description: function on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local Parts = { 'return ', '1 + 1' }
local I = 0
local Chunk = load(function() I = I + 1 return Parts[I] end)
print(Chunk())  -- 2

items.name: getfenv
items.description: Returns the current environment table of f (a function, or a stack-level integer; default 1, the calling function).

examples.code: local Env = getfenv(1)

items.name: setfenv
items.description: Sets the environment for the function f (a function, or a stack-level integer, where 1 means the calling function) to table. Returns f when f is a function.

examples.code:
local Sandbox = setmetatable({}, { __index = _G })
setfenv(SomeFn, Sandbox)

items.name: module
items.summary: Create or enter a named module.
items.description: Legacy Lua 5.1 module system: creates (or reuses) a table for module name, sets it as the value of the global name and of package.loaded[name], and sets it as the new environment of the running function, so subsequent top-level function/variable definitions become fields of the module. Optional arguments are 'module modifiers' such as package.seeall. Superseded in most modern Lua code by returning a table from a plain chunk loaded via require.

examples.code:
module('mymodule', package.seeall)

function greet(name)
   return 'hello, ' .. name
end

modules.name: linkiir.data
modules.title: Message Data
modules.description: Parse (extract), build (create), and serialize messages of any supported format (HL7, X12, XML), plus the node-tree interface returned by those calls. XML supports schema-free parsing (schema optional).

items.name: linkiir.data.extract
items.summary: Parse a wire message into a node tree.
items.description: Parse a raw wire message into a Linkiir node tree, identify the matched message definition from the grammar, and return both. The tree is read/write.

params.name: data
params.description: Raw message text (HL7 v2, X12, XML, or JSON).

params.name: type
params.description: Protocol override: "hl7", "x12", "xml", "json". Defaults to the grammar's protocol.

returns.name: node
returns.description: root of the parsed tree (Linkiir node) — see the Node:* methods in this module.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure (trap with pcall).

examples.code:
local Msg, MsgType = linkiir.data.extract{ schema = 'demo.json', data = Data, type = 'hl7' }
print(MsgType)                               -- "ADT"
print(Msg.MSH[9][1]:value(), Msg.PID[3][1][1]:value())

-- Trap failures explicitly.
local ok, msg, mtype = pcall(linkiir.data.extract, { schema = 'demo.json', data = Data })
if not ok then error('extract failed: ' .. tostring(msg)) end

items.name: linkiir.data.create
items.summary: Build an empty message tree for a definition.
items.description: Create an empty message tree for a named grammar definition, with all schema segments/groups/fields pre-allocated so they can be populated by assignment or :map.

params.name: name
params.description: Grammar message-definition name (usually the 2nd return of linkiir.data.extract).

params.name: type
params.description: Protocol override; defaults to the grammar's protocol.

returns.name: node
returns.description: root of the empty message tree — see the Node:* methods in this module.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

items.name: linkiir.data.serialize
items.summary: Serialize a node tree back to wire text.
items.description: Serialize a node tree back to its wire representation (HL7 pipe-delimited text, X12 segment stream, etc.). Equivalent to node:text() / node:S().

params.name: data
params.description: The node to serialize (root or subtree).

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

examples.code:
local wire  = linkiir.data.serialize{ data = Out }
local wire2 = Out:text()   -- identical result

items.name: Node:value
items.description: Scalar value of the node.

examples.code:
local N = Msg.PID[3][1][1]
local V = N:value()
print(V)

items.name: Node:set
items.description: Set the scalar value (chainable).

examples.code:
N:set('12345')       -- write a new scalar value
print(N:value())    -- "12345"

items.name: Node:name
items.description: Node/segment name.

examples.code: print(N:name())  -- e.g. "PID"

items.name: Node:text
items.summary: Serialize the subtree to wire text.
items.description: Serialize the subtree to wire text.

examples.code: local Wire = N:text()  -- serialize this subtree back to wire format

items.name: Node:map
items.description: Copy matching values from src.

params.name: src
params.description: Source node to copy matching values from.

examples.code:
local Out = linkiir.data.create{ schema = 'demo.json', name = MsgType }
Out:map(Msg)  -- copy matching values from Msg into Out

items.name: Node:child
items.summary: Child by name or 1-based index (= Node[k]).
items.description: Child by name or 1-based index (= Node[k]).

examples.code: local Field = Msg.PID:child(3)  -- same as Msg.PID[3]

items.name: Node:count
items.description: Number of children (= #Node).

examples.code: print(#Msg.PID)  -- same as Msg.PID:count()

items.name: Node:isNull
items.summary: True when the node has no data.
items.description: True when the node has no data.

examples.code:
if Msg.PID[5]:isNull() then
   print('no patient name present')
end

items.name: Node:isLeaf
items.summary: True when the node holds a scalar.
items.description: True when the node holds a scalar.

examples.code: print(N:isLeaf())  -- true when N holds a scalar value

items.name: Node:type
items.description: Node type code (1..6, 10..13, 99).

examples.code: print(N:type())  -- node type code

items.name: Node:protocol
items.description: Protocol code (101 HL7 … 105 XML).

examples.code: print(Msg:protocol())  -- 101 (HL7), 102 (X12), 105 (XML), ...

items.name: linkiir.data.codeset.get
items.summary: Load a code set from a schema.
items.description: Retrieve a code set (Table object) from the given schema by its id. Returns nil when the code set id is not present in the schema — callers can branch without pcall. The schema path resolves relative to the current node directory, the same as linkiir.data.extract.

params.name: schema
params.description: Linkiir grammar JSON file containing the code set (e.g. demo.json).

params.name: table
params.description: Code set id to look up (e.g. "0001").

returns.name: Table
returns.description: Table userdata for the code set, or nil if the id is absent from the schema.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure (trap with pcall).

examples.code:
local codeset = linkiir.data.codeset
local Sex = codeset.get{ schema = 'demo.json', table = '0001' }
if Sex then
  print('Loaded code set 0001 with ' .. #Sex:codes() .. ' codes')
else
  print('Code set 0001 not found in schema')
end

-- Raises on missing parameter or unloadable schema.
local ok, err = pcall(codeset.get, { schema = 'missing.json', table = '0001' })
if not ok then print(err) end

items.name: linkiir.data.codeset.match
items.summary: Map source code values to destination code values by description.
items.description: Build a plain Lua table that maps each source code value to the destination code value whose description matches (case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed). Source codes with no matching description in the destination are omitted — use an 'or default' fallback at the call site to handle gaps. Cross-format mapping is intentionally the developer's job; match provides description-based joining to automate the common case, while developers handle the remaining gaps via fallback values or manual overrides.

params.name: sourceTable
params.description: Source code set (Table userdata returned by table.get).

params.name: destTable
params.description: Destination code set (Table userdata returned by table.get).

returns.name: map
returns.description: Plain Lua table keyed by source code values, values are destination code values. Assignable, printable, pairs-able.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error if either argument is not a Table userdata.

items.name: Table:codes
items.summary: All code values in stored order.
items.description: Return an array of all code value strings in the code set, preserving the order defined in the schema (spec order or drag-reordered).

examples.code:
local codeset = linkiir.data.codeset
local Sex = codeset.get{ schema = 'demo.json', table = '0001' }
for i, code in ipairs(Sex:codes()) do
  print(i, code)   -- 1 F, 2 M, 3 O, ...
end

items.name: Table:pairs
items.usage: for code, desc in T:pairs() do ... end
items.description: Return an iterator that yields (code, description) pairs in stored order. Suitable for use in a generic for loop.

examples.code:
local codeset = linkiir.data.codeset
local Sex = codeset.get{ schema = 'demo.json', table = '0001' }
for code, desc in Sex:pairs() do
  print(code .. ' = ' .. desc)   -- F = Female, M = Male, ...
end

items.name: Table:desc
items.summary: Look up the description for a code value.
items.description: Return the description string for the given code value, or nil if the code is not present in this code set. Builds an internal index on first call for efficient repeated lookups.

returns.name: desc
returns.description: Description string (e.g. "Female"), or nil if the code is not in the code set.

examples.code:
local codeset = linkiir.data.codeset
local Sex = codeset.get{ schema = 'demo.json', table = '0001' }
print(Sex:desc('F'))    -- "Female"
print(Sex:desc('X'))    -- nil (not in code set)

modules.name: linkiir.flow
modules.title: Message Flow
modules.description: Everything about a message's movement through a channel: acknowledge what came in, route/enqueue what goes out.

items.name: linkiir.flow.push
items.usage: linkiir.flow.push{ data = <string> [, topic=] [, metadata=] [, live=] }   -- or linkiir.flow.push(<string>)
items.description: Enqueue/route a message to the next Linkiir node/topic and return its trace id.

params.name: topic
params.description: Target topic/node; defaults to the configured destination.

params.name: metadata
params.description: Key/value headers stored with the message.

returns.name: messageId (string)
returns.description: Linkiir trace id assigned at enqueue.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

examples.code: local MessageId = linkiir.flow.push{ data = Out:text(), topic = 'adt.out' }

items.name: linkiir.flow.configure
items.signature: linkiir.flow.configure{ bootstrap=, project=, workflow=, node=, topic= }
items.usage: linkiir.flow.configure{ project = <string> [, workflow=] [, node=] [, bootstrap=] [, topic=] }
items.summary: Configure the flow context (node identity and Kafka settings).
items.description: Configure the flow context (node identity and Kafka settings). Non-empty fields override the current value; empty fields are left unchanged. Context is also initialized from environment variables (LINKIIR_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP, LINKIIR_PROJECT_ID, LINKIIR_WORKFLOW_ID, LINKIIR_NODE_ID, LINKIIR_OUTPUT_TOPIC).

examples.code: linkiir.flow.configure{ project = "ADT", workflow = "InboundHL7", node = "Transform1" }

items.name: linkiir.flow.topic
items.summary: Return the resolved output topic name (or nil if unresolvable).
items.description: Return the resolved output topic name (or nil if unresolvable). Resolution order: explicit topic from configure() > LINKIIR_OUTPUT_TOPIC env > derived "linkiir.node.<project>.<workflow>.<node>".

returns.name: topic
returns.description: Resolved topic name (string), or nil if unresolvable.

examples.code: print(linkiir.flow.topic())  -- "linkiir.node.ADT.InboundHL7.Transform1"

modules.name: linkiir.link
modules.title: Connectivity
modules.description: All connectivity to external systems, named for the heart of Linkiir. Sub-areas: web (HTTP), socket (TCP), mail (SMTP), file (FTP/FTPS/SFTP). All calls return result, err.

items.name: linkiir.link.web.get
items.signature: linkiir.link.web.get{ url=, headers=, params=, body=, auth=, timeout=, tls=, verifyTls=, live= }
items.usage: linkiir.link.web.get{ url=, headers=, params=, body=, auth=, timeout=, tls=, verifyTls=, live= }
items.summary: Perform an outbound HTTP GET request.
items.description: Perform an outbound HTTP GET request. The tls sub-table is supported identically on all seven verbs (get, post, put, patch, delete, head, options), which share one request path.

params.name: tls
params.description: Client certificate for mutual TLS (mTLS): { certFile=, keyFile=, caFile= }. All three are filesystem paths to PEM files - certificate or key material is never accepted inline, so a private key never enters script memory. PEM is the only accepted format, matching the Linkiir web server's Certificate File and Private Key File settings; convert a PKCS#12 bundle or an encrypted key once with openssl before use. certFile and keyFile must be supplied together. caFile pins the trust anchor for verifying the server and may be used with or without a client certificate; it does not disable verification, which stays with verifyTls. Relative paths resolve against the working directory and may not escape it; absolute paths are used unchanged. Each path must be a readable file or the call raises before any request is made.

returns.description: resp = { code=<int>, body=<string>, headers=<table> } on success

errors.description: Returns result, err (err = { code=, message= }).

examples.code:
-- mTLS applies to every verb, not just post: the tls sub-table is read on
-- one shared request path. Here it is on a read, with a bearer token.
local Resp, Err = linkiir.link.web.get{
   url    = Cfg.pcc_api_base .. '/orgs/' .. Cfg.pcc_org_uuid .. '/patients',
   params = { facId = Cfg.pcc_fac_id },
   auth   = { type = 'bearer', token = Token },
   tls    = { certFile = Cfg.pcc_cert_file,   -- 0644
              keyFile  = Cfg.pcc_key_file },  -- 0600
}
if not Resp then error('transport failure: ' .. Err.code) end
if Resp.code ~= 200 then error('lookup rejected: HTTP ' .. Resp.code) end

items.name: linkiir.link.web.post
items.signature: linkiir.link.web.post{ url=, headers=, params=, body=, auth=, timeout=, tls=, verifyTls=, live= }
items.usage: linkiir.link.web.post{ url=, headers=, params=, body=, auth=, timeout=, tls=, verifyTls=, live= }
items.summary: Perform an outbound HTTP POST request.
items.description: Perform an outbound HTTP POST request, sending `body` as the request payload. The tls sub-table is supported identically on all seven verbs (get, post, put, patch, delete, head, options), which share one request path.

params.name: tls
params.description: Client certificate for mutual TLS (mTLS): { certFile=, keyFile=, caFile= }. All three are filesystem paths to PEM files - certificate or key material is never accepted inline, so a private key never enters script memory. PEM is the only accepted format, matching the Linkiir web server's Certificate File and Private Key File settings; convert a PKCS#12 bundle or an encrypted key once with openssl before use. certFile and keyFile must be supplied together. caFile pins the trust anchor for verifying the server and may be used with or without a client certificate; it does not disable verification, which stays with verifyTls. Relative paths resolve against the working directory and may not escape it; absolute paths are used unchanged. Each path must be a readable file or the call raises before any request is made.

returns.description: resp = { code=<int>, body=<string>, headers=<table> } on success

errors.description: Returns result, err (err = { code=, message= }).

examples.code:
local Resp, Err = linkiir.link.web.post{
   url     = 'https://fhir.example.com/Patient',
   headers = { ['Content-Type'] = 'application/fhir+json' },
   body    = linkiir.data.serialize{ data = Out },
   auth    = { type = 'bearer', token = Token },
}
if not Resp then error(Err.message) end
print(Resp.code, Resp.body)

-- Two-legged OAuth over mTLS: HTTP Basic *and* a client certificate on
-- the same request, then a bearer token plus the same certificate.
-- Recommended permissions: certificate 0644, private key 0600, both
-- outside any project directory so they never enter a project repository.
local Cfg = linkiir.config.node()
local Tls = { certFile = Cfg.pcc_cert_file,   -- certs/pcc-client.pem
              keyFile  = Cfg.pcc_key_file }   -- certs/pcc-client.key

local Resp, Err = linkiir.link.web.post{
   url     = Cfg.pcc_token_url,
   auth    = { type = 'basic', user = Cfg.pcc_client_id,
               password = Cfg.pcc_client_secret },
   headers = { ['Content-Type'] = 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
   body    = 'grant_type=client_credentials',
   timeout = 20,

modules.description: Database access, named for what it does (store / retrieve). Connection-object style only; query results are Linkiir node trees (protocol code 103 = DB).

items.name: linkiir.store.open
items.signature: linkiir.store.open{ driver=, name=, user=, password=, live= }
items.usage: local conn, err = linkiir.store.open{ driver=, name=, user=, password=, timeout=, live= }
items.description: Open a database connection. Pass one of the driver constants (linkiir.store.SQLITE, MYSQL, MARIADB, ORACLE, POSTGRES_ODBC, SQLSERVER_ODBC, ORACLE_ODBC, MYSQL_ODBC) as the driver parameter.

params.name: driver
params.description: One of the linkiir.store.* driver constants (e.g. linkiir.store.SQLITE). These are integer values, not strings.

params.name: name
params.description: DSN / host / database / file, per driver. For SQLITE this is a file path: a relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), never the process working directory, and an absolute path is used unchanged. The :memory: sentinel and file: URIs are passed to SQLite untouched. For every other driver the value is a server, DSN or database name and is never treated as a path.

returns.description: conn (connection object) on success — see the Connection:* methods in this module.

errors.description: Returns result, err.

modules.name: linkiir.json
modules.title: JSON
modules.description: JSON parse and serialize operating on plain Lua tables. Unlike linkiir.data, which returns the node-tree interface, linkiir.json works with native Lua values. json.array() and json.object() tag a table so its JSON shape is explicit rather than inferred.

items.name: linkiir.json.parse
items.summary: Parse a JSON string into a Lua value.
items.description: Parse a JSON string into a Lua value. Objects become tables with string keys; arrays become tables with integer keys 1..N. JSON null becomes linkiir.json.null. Raises on invalid JSON.

returns.description: Lua value: table (object/array), string, number, boolean, or json.null.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

examples.code:
local obj = linkiir.json.parse('{"name":"Alice","age":30}')
print(obj.name)  -- "Alice"
print(obj.age)   -- 30

items.name: linkiir.json.serialize
items.summary: Serialize a Lua value to a JSON string.
items.description: Serialize a Lua value to a JSON string. Tables with consecutive integer keys emit as arrays; otherwise as objects, unless the table was tagged with linkiir.json.array() or linkiir.json.object(). nil and json.null become null. Raises on circular references, NaN/Infinity, or non-serializable types (functions, userdata).

params.name: value
params.description: Lua value to serialize (table, string, number, boolean, nil, json.null).

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

examples.code:
local s = linkiir.json.serialize({name = "Alice", age = 30})
print(s)  -- {"name":"Alice","age":30}

items.name: linkiir.json.array
items.summary: Tag a table so it always serializes as a JSON array.
items.description: Mark a Lua table as a JSON array. Called with no argument (or nil) it creates and tags a new empty table; called with a table it tags that table in place and returns it. The tag overrides the usual shape heuristic, so a tagged table emits as [ ... ] even when empty or when it holds string keys (array serialization walks integer keys 1..N and ignores the rest). Tables returned by linkiir.json.parse are already tagged, so an empty array survives a parse/serialize round-trip.

params.name: t
params.description: Existing table to tag. Omit or pass nil to create a new empty table.

returns.description: The tagged table (the same table when one was passed in).

errors.description: Raises a Lua error if the argument is present and not a table.

items.name: linkiir.json.object
items.summary: Tag a table so it always serializes as a JSON object.
items.description: Mark a Lua table as a JSON object. Called with no argument (or nil) it creates and tags a new empty table; called with a table it tags that table in place and returns it. The tag overrides the usual shape heuristic: an untagged empty table serializes as [], while a tagged one serializes as {}. A tagged table holding a sequence emits its integer keys as the object keys "1", "2", ... Tables returned by linkiir.json.parse are already tagged.

params.name: t
params.description: Existing table to tag. Omit or pass nil to create a new empty table.

returns.description: The tagged table (the same table when one was passed in).

errors.description: Raises a Lua error if the argument is present and not a table.

items.name: linkiir.json.null
items.usage: if obj.x == linkiir.json.null then print('null') end
items.description: A unique sentinel table that represents JSON null. Distinguishes 'key is null' (obj.x == json.null) from 'key is absent' (obj.x == nil). Serializes as null.

examples.code:
local obj = linkiir.json.parse('{"x": null}')
assert(obj.x == linkiir.json.null)  -- present but null
assert(obj.y == nil)                -- truly absent

modules.name: linkiir.sys
modules.title: Runtime & System
modules.description: Small runtime helpers and filesystem access in one place. Time/env helpers (os.date, os.time, os.getenv) stay as native Lua. Path resolution: every linkiir.sys.fs function resolves a relative path against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), never the process working directory. An absolute path is used unchanged. A relative path that escapes the working directory via .. is rejected.

items.name: linkiir.sys.guid
items.summary: Generate a random GUID of the requested bit length.
items.description: Generate a random GUID. The bit count is required: it must be at least 128 and divisible by 8. Calling guid() with no argument, or with fewer than 128 bits, raises a Lua error.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

examples.code:
local Id  = linkiir.sys.guid(128)   -- 128-bit GUID
local Big = linkiir.sys.guid(256)   -- 256 bits when more entropy is wanted
-- linkiir.sys.guid()   -- error: bits is required
-- linkiir.sys.guid(32) -- error: must be at least 128 bits

params.name: bits
params.description: Length in bits. Minimum 128, must be divisible by 8.

items.name: linkiir.sys.sleep
items.description: Pause the current run for the given number of milliseconds.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error on failure.

examples.code: linkiir.sys.sleep(250)

items.name: linkiir.sys.workingDir
items.summary: Absolute path of the Runtime's working directory.
items.description: Absolute path of the Runtime's working directory - the parent of projects/, users/, logs/ and run/. This is the base a relative linkiir.store or linkiir.sys.fs path resolves against, so a project built on it means the same thing regardless of how the service was started. Returns the same value under Run Test and Debug as the live Runtime reports for that node.

returns.name: string
returns.description: absolute path to the working directory.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error naming the missing context when the working directory is unknown to the calling VM, rather than returning an empty string.

examples.code:
local Root = linkiir.sys.workingDir()
print('working dir: ' .. Root)

-- Rarely needed: a relative path already resolves here.
local DB = linkiir.store.open{ driver = linkiir.store.SQLITE, name = 'demo/patient.db' }

items.name: linkiir.sys.nodeDir
items.summary: Absolute path of the executing node's directory.
items.description: Absolute path of the directory the executing node's files were loaded from. Under the live Runtime this is the staged run folder; under Run Test and Debug it is your dev clone. Replaces the deprecated __node_dir global. A relative schema path already resolves against this directory, so concatenation is not needed.

returns.name: string
returns.description: absolute path to the node directory.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error naming the missing context when the node directory is unknown to the calling VM.

examples.code:
local Dir = linkiir.sys.nodeDir()
print('node dir: ' .. Dir)

-- Rarely needed: a relative schema path already resolves here.
local Msg = linkiir.data.extract{ schema = 'demo.json', data = Data }

modules.name: linkiir.log
modules.title: Logging
modules.description: Emit structured log events to the workflow event topic. Each call produces a SCRIPT_LOG record at the named level. These are annotations — they never raise, never stop the node, and are independent of Lua's error(). Gated by the node's log_level setting: a call below the threshold is dropped inside the runtime and never reaches the broker.

items.name: linkiir.log.error
items.summary: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at ERROR level.
items.description: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at ERROR level. Does not stop the node (unlike Lua's error()). This is an annotation, not a fault — it never raises, never halts execution. Gated by the node's log_level setting.

examples.code: linkiir.log.error('Failed to parse inbound HL7: ' .. tostring(Err))

items.name: linkiir.log.warn
items.summary: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at WARN level.
items.description: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at WARN level. This is an annotation, not a fault — it never raises, never halts execution. Gated by the node's log_level setting.

examples.code: linkiir.log.warn('Missing optional field PID[8], defaulting to Unknown')

items.name: linkiir.log.info
items.summary: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at INFO level.
items.description: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at INFO level. This is an annotation, not a fault — it never raises, never halts execution. Gated by the node's log_level setting.

examples.code: linkiir.log.info('Processed ' .. tostring(Count) .. ' segments')

items.name: linkiir.log.debug
items.summary: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at DEBUG level.
items.description: Emit a SCRIPT_LOG event at DEBUG level. Dropped by the runtime if the node's log_level is above DEBUG. This is an annotation, not a fault — it never raises, never halts execution. Gated by the node's log_level setting.

examples.code: linkiir.log.debug('Raw payload length: ' .. tostring(#Data))

modules.name: linkiir.config
modules.title: Node Configuration
modules.description: Read the current node's configuration fields. Values come from the config fields set on the node in the Node Parameters panel, flattened into a single label → value table. Password fields are decrypted automatically. The result is cached for the lifetime of the script VM: the first call reads and parses the configuration, every later call returns the same table with no I/O.

items.name: linkiir.config.node
items.summary: Return this node's configuration as a label → value table.
items.description: Reads the current node's configuration and returns a flat table keyed by each config entry's label. Strings, numbers, and booleans map straight across. Labels that are absent, null, or hold an object or array read as nil. The table is cached per script VM: the configuration is read once, and every later call returns that same table.

returns.name: table
returns.description: flat map of config label → value (string, number, or boolean); empty when the node has no config fields.

errors.description: Raises a Lua error when the node directory is not configured, when the node's configuration is missing or unreadable, when it is malformed, or when a password field cannot be decrypted (typically a missing or wrong LINKIIR_SECRET_KEY).

examples.code:
local Cfg = linkiir.config.node()

local Host = Cfg.host          -- "10.0.0.1"
local Port = Cfg.port          -- 2575 (number)
local UseSsl = Cfg.use_ssl     -- true (boolean)
local Password = Cfg.password  -- decrypted plaintext

local Sock, Err = linkiir.link.socket.connect{ host = Host, port = Port }
if not Sock then
  linkiir.log.error('connect failed: ' .. tostring(Err))
  return
end

-- Absent fields are nil, so defaults are a plain 'or'.
local Cfg = linkiir.config.node()
local Timeout = Cfg.timeout_ms or 5000

if Cfg.protocol == 'hl7' then
  linkiir.log.info('Using HL7 profile')
end

-- Cached: the second call does no disk I/O and returns the same table.
local A = linkiir.config.node()
local B = linkiir.config.node()
assert(rawequal(A, B))

modules.name: table
modules.title: Lua Table Library
modules.description: Standard Lua 5.1 table library for building and manipulating array-style tables (insert/remove/sort/concat). Node trees returned by linkiir.data are their own object type, not plain tables — use the Node:* methods for those.

items.name: table.insert
items.summary: Insert an element into a table.
items.description: Inserts value at position pos in table t, shifting up subsequent elements. pos defaults to #t + 1 (append to the end).

items.name: table.remove
items.summary: Remove an element from a table.
items.description: Removes from table t the element at position pos, shifting down subsequent elements, and returns the removed value. pos defaults to #t (remove the last element).

items.name: table.concat
items.summary: Join array elements into a string.
items.description: Returns t[i] .. sep .. t[i+1] .. sep .. ... .. t[j]. sep defaults to the empty string; i defaults to 1; j defaults to #t.

examples.code:
local Ids = { '1', '2', '3' }
print(table.concat(Ids, ','))  -- "1,2,3"

items.name: table.sort
items.summary: Sort a table's array part in place.
items.description: Sorts the elements of table t (the array part) in place, from t[1] to t[#t]. comp is an optional less-than comparator function; the default is the standard `<` operator.

params.name: comp
params.description: Comparator: function(a, b) returning true when a should come before b.

examples.code:
local Nums = { 3, 1, 2 }
table.sort(Nums)
print(table.concat(Nums, ','))  -- "1,2,3"

table.sort(Nums, function(a, b) return a > b end)  -- descending

items.name: table.maxn
items.summary: Largest positive numeric key in a table.
items.description: Returns the largest positive numerical index of table t, or 0 if t has no positive numerical indices. Useful for arrays with holes, where #t is undefined.

examples.code:
local Sparse = { [1] = 'a', [5] = 'b' }
print(table.maxn(Sparse))  -- 5

modules.name: os
modules.title: Lua OS Library (time/env)
modules.description: Time and environment functions from the standard Lua 5.1 os library, plus the file/process functions (os.execute, os.remove, os.rename, os.tmpname, os.exit). The file/process functions are fully functional but are a Linkiir convention to avoid in workflow scripts — they bypass logging/auditing and portability that linkiir.sys.fs (local filesystem) and linkiir.link.file (remote transfer) provide, and os.exit()/os.execute() can terminate or fork the worker process outright. Prefer the linkiir.* equivalents unless you specifically need raw OS access. os.remove and os.rename resolve paths the same way as linkiir.sys.fs: a relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path that escapes the working directory via '..' raises an error. os.execute, os.exit and os.tmpname are unwrapped and still act on the raw process.

items.name: os.time
items.summary: Current time / convert a date table to a timestamp.
items.description: With no arguments, returns the current time as a Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch). With a date table ({year=, month=, day=, hour=, min=, sec=}), returns the corresponding timestamp.

examples.code:
print(os.time())
print(os.time({ year = 2026, month = 1, day = 1 }))

items.name: os.date
items.description: Returns a string (or a table, if format starts with "*t") describing the date/time given by time (default now), formatted per strftime-style format (default "%c").

params.name: format
params.description: strftime-style format, or "*t"/"!*t" for a date table. Default "%c".

returns.description: string, or table when format is "*t"/"!*t"

examples.code:
print(os.date('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'))
local T = os.date('*t')
print(T.year, T.month, T.day)

items.name: os.clock
items.summary: CPU time used by the process.
items.description: Returns an approximation of the amount of CPU time used by the program, in seconds. Useful for benchmarking script execution.

examples.code:
local Start = os.clock()
-- ... work ...
print('elapsed', os.clock() - Start)

items.name: os.difftime
items.description: Returns the number of seconds from time t1 to time t2 (both Unix timestamps, as returned by os.time).

examples.code: local Elapsed = os.difftime(os.time(), StartedAt)

items.name: os.getenv
items.description: Returns the value of the process environment variable varname, or nil if it is not set.

examples.code: local ApiKey = os.getenv('LINKIIR_API_KEY')

items.name: os.execute
items.description: Passes command to the system shell (via C's system()) and returns its exit status. With no argument, returns whether a shell is available. Runs with the worker process's OS privileges — discouraged in workflow scripts; prefer linkiir.sys.fs / linkiir.link.file for file and transfer work.

returns.description: integer exit status (or boolean shell-availability when called with no arguments)

examples.code:
local Status = os.execute('true')
print(Status)  -- 0

items.name: os.remove
items.description: Deletes the file (or empty directory, on POSIX) at filename. Returns true on success, or nil plus an error message on failure. Prefer linkiir.sys.fs.remove, which is scoped to the node's working directories. A relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), not the process working directory; an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path escaping the working directory via '..' raises an error.

params.name: filename
params.description: Path of the file to delete.

returns.description: true on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local Ok, Err = os.remove('/tmp/scratch.txt')
if not Ok then print(Err) end

items.name: os.rename
items.description: Renames the file or directory at oldname to newname. Returns true on success, or nil plus an error message on failure. A relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), not the process working directory; an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path escaping the working directory via '..' raises an error.

returns.description: true on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local Ok, Err = os.rename('/tmp/a.txt', '/tmp/b.txt')
if not Ok then print(Err) end

items.name: os.tmpname
items.description: Returns a string with a name that can safely be used as a temporary file. The file must be explicitly opened (e.g. io.open) and removed (os.remove) when done.

examples.code:
local Path = os.tmpname()
local F = io.open(Path, 'w')
F:write('scratch')
F:close()
os.remove(Path)

items.name: os.exit
items.description: Terminates the host process immediately, with an optional exit code (default success/true) and an optional flag to close the Lua state first. Never call this in a workflow script — it kills the worker process running the script, not just the current script invocation.

params.name: close
params.description: Whether to close the Lua state before exiting. Default false.

examples.code:
-- Avoid in Linkiir scripts; shown for reference only.
-- os.exit(0)

modules.name: io
modules.title: Lua IO Library (files/stdio)
modules.description: Standard Lua 5.1 io library: local file and standard-stream I/O, available exactly as in stock Lua/LuaJIT (registered by the runtime alongside table/math/os/string). For directory listings, metadata, and simple file management, prefer linkiir.sys.fs, which is purpose-built for the node's working directories; for reading/writing remote files (FTP/SFTP), use linkiir.link.file. io.* is the right tool when you need actual byte-level read/write access to a local file or stdin/stdout/stderr. io.popen spawns a shell process and should be avoided in workflow scripts. Paths are resolved the same way as linkiir.sys.fs: io.open, io.lines, io.input and io.output take a relative path as relative to the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), never the process working directory. Absolute paths are used unchanged, and a relative path that escapes the working directory via '..' raises an error.

items.name: io.open
items.description: Opens filename in the given mode ("r" read, "w" write/truncate, "a" append, with optional "b" for binary and "+" for update; default "r"). Returns a new file handle on success, or nil plus an error message on failure. A relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), not the process working directory; an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path escaping the working directory via '..' raises an error.

params.name: mode
params.description: r/w/a, optionally with b and/or +. Default "r".

returns.description: file handle on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local F, Err = io.open(linkiir.sys.nodeDir() .. '/scratch.txt', 'w')
if not F then error(Err) end
F:write('hello')
F:close()

items.name: io.close
items.description: Closes file (default the current default output file). Equivalent to file:close().

params.name: file
params.description: File handle to close. Default the current output file.

returns.description: true on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local F = io.open('/tmp/x.txt', 'r')
-- ... use F ...
io.close(F)

items.name: io.read
items.summary: Read from the default input file.
items.description: Reads from the current default input file, using the same formats as file:read.

params.description: Format specifiers ("*l", "*n", "*a", or a byte count). Default "*l".

returns.description: the values read, per format; nil at end of file

examples.code: local Line = io.read('*l')

items.name: io.write
items.summary: Write to the default output file.
items.description: Writes the given strings/numbers to the current default output file, using the same rules as file:write.

returns.description: the default output file, for chaining; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code: io.write('processed ', tostring(Count), ' records\n')

items.name: io.lines
items.usage: for line in io.lines(filename) do ... end
items.summary: Iterate the lines of a file.
items.description: Opens filename (or uses the default input file if omitted), and returns an iterator function that returns a new line each time it is called, per the given format(s). The file is closed automatically when the iterator finishes (only when a filename is given). A relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), not the process working directory; an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path escaping the working directory via '..' raises an error.

params.name: filename
params.description: Path to read. Default the current input file.

returns.description: iterator function, for use in a generic for loop

examples.code:
for Line in io.lines(linkiir.sys.nodeDir() .. '/data.csv') do
   print(Line)
end

items.name: io.input
items.description: With a string, opens the named file in read mode and sets it as the default input file. With a file handle, sets it as the default input file. With no argument, returns the current default input file. A relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), not the process working directory; an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path escaping the working directory via '..' raises an error.

params.name: file
params.description: Filename to open, or an already-open file handle.

examples.code:
io.input(linkiir.sys.nodeDir() .. '/data.csv')
local Line = io.read('*l')

items.name: io.output
items.description: With a string, opens the named file in write mode and sets it as the default output file. With a file handle, sets it as the default output file. With no argument, returns the current default output file. A relative path resolves against the Runtime's working directory (linkiir.sys.workingDir()), not the process working directory; an absolute path is used unchanged, and a path escaping the working directory via '..' raises an error.

params.name: file
params.description: Filename to open, or an already-open file handle.

examples.code:
io.output('/tmp/out.txt')
io.write('done\n')

items.name: io.popen
items.summary: Run a shell command, connected via a pipe.
items.description: Starts prog in a separate process (via the system shell) and returns a file handle for reading its output (mode "r", the default) or writing to its input (mode "w"). Runs with the worker process's OS privileges — avoid in workflow scripts; prefer linkiir.link.file / linkiir.link.web for external I/O.

params.name: mode
params.description: "r" (read prog's stdout) or "w" (write to prog's stdin). Default "r".

returns.description: file handle on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
-- Avoid in Linkiir scripts; shown for reference only.
local P = io.popen('date', 'r')
print(P:read('*l'))
P:close()

items.name: io.tmpfile
items.description: Returns a handle for a temporary file, opened in update mode ('w+'), that is automatically removed when the script ends.

returns.description: file handle on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local F = io.tmpfile()
F:write('scratch')
F:seek('set', 0)
print(F:read('*a'))

items.name: io.type
items.summary: Test whether a value is a file handle.
items.description: Returns "file" if obj is an open file handle, "closed file" if it is a closed file handle, or nil if it is not a file handle at all.

examples.code:
local F = io.open('/tmp/x.txt', 'r')
print(io.type(F))  -- "file"
F:close()
print(io.type(F))  -- "closed file"

items.name: io.stdin
items.summary: The process's standard input file handle.
items.description: The process's standard input, as a file handle.

examples.code: local Line = io.stdin:read('*l')

items.name: io.stdout
items.summary: The process's standard output file handle.
items.description: The process's standard output, as a file handle.

examples.code: io.stdout:write('hello\n')

items.name: io.stderr
items.summary: The process's standard error file handle.
items.description: The process's standard error, as a file handle.

examples.code: io.stderr:write('warning: retrying\n')

items.name: File:read
items.description: Reads from file per the given format(s): "*l" a line without the newline (default), "*L" a line with the newline, "*a" the whole rest of the file, "*n" a number, or an integer n for up to n bytes. Returns nil (or an empty string for "*a") at end of file.

returns.description: the value(s) read, one per format; nil at end of file

params.description: One or more read formats. Default "*l".

examples.code:
local F = io.open(Path, 'r')
local All = F:read('*a')
F:close()

items.name: File:write
items.description: Writes the given strings/numbers to file. Numbers are converted per their usual string representation.

returns.description: file, for chaining; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local F = io.open(Path, 'w')
F:write('id,name\n')
F:write('1,Alice\n')
F:close()

items.name: File:close
items.description: Closes file. Files are also closed automatically (in an unspecified order) when their handle is garbage-collected, but explicit close is recommended.

returns.description: true on success; nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local F = io.open(Path, 'r')
-- ... use F ...
F:close()

items.name: File:lines
items.summary: Iterate the lines of an already-open file.
items.description: Returns an iterator function that, each time it is called, reads the next line from file per the given format(s) (as file:read; default "*l"). Does not close file when done.

returns.description: iterator function, for use in a generic for loop

items.usage: for line in f:lines() do ... end

examples.code:
local F = io.open(Path, 'r')
for Line in F:lines() do
   print(Line)
end
F:close()

items.name: File:seek
items.description: Sets and/or gets the current file position, measured from the start of the file. whence is "set" (from the start), "cur" (from the current position, the default), or "end" (from the end of the file); offset defaults to 0. With no arguments, returns the current position without changing it.

returns.description: the new file position (bytes from the start); nil, errorMessage on failure

examples.code:
local F = io.open(Path, 'r')
local Size = F:seek('end')
F:seek('set', 0)
F:close()

items.name: File:flush
items.description: Saves any written data to file, without closing it.

examples.code:
F:write('partial')
F:flush()

items.name: File:setvbuf
items.description: Sets the buffering mode for an output file: "no" (unbuffered), "full" (buffer up to size bytes, flushed when full or explicitly), or "line" (line-buffered).

examples.code: F:setvbuf('line')

modules.name: string
modules.title: Lua String Library
modules.description: Standard Lua 5.1 string library. Available as both `string.fn(s, ...)` and object-style `s:fn(...)`, since every string has a metatable pointing back to this table. Pattern-matching functions (find, match, gmatch, gsub) use Lua patterns, not full regular expressions.

items.name: string.byte
items.summary: Numeric byte codes of characters s[i..j].
items.description: Returns the internal numeric codes of the characters s[i], s[i+1], ..., s[j]. The default for i is 1; the default for j is i.

params.name: i
params.description: Start index (1-based, negative counts from the end). Default 1.

returns.description: one integer per byte in range i..j

examples.code:
print(string.byte('A'))        -- 65
print(('ABC'):byte(1, 3))      -- 65 66 67

items.name: string.char
items.summary: Build a string from numeric byte codes.
items.description: Receives zero or more integers and returns a string with a character for each code.

examples.code: print(string.char(65, 66, 67))  -- "ABC"

items.name: string.dump
items.summary: Serialize a function to a binary chunk.
items.description: Returns a binary string containing a loadable, compiled representation (bytecode) of function. To load and run it again, pass the string to loadstring (or load). Only works on Lua functions defined in the script itself, not C functions exposed by the runtime (print, linkiir.*, etc.).

params.name: function
params.description: A Lua function with no upvalues other than _ENV/globals.

examples.code:
local function Add(a, b) return a + b end
local Bytes = string.dump(Add)
local Reloaded = loadstring(Bytes)
print(Reloaded(2, 3))  -- 5

items.name: string.find
items.summary: Find the first match of a pattern in a string.
items.description: Looks for the first match of pattern in s, starting search at position init. Returns the start and end indices of the match, plus any captures. Returns nil if no match. If plain is true, pattern is matched as a literal substring (no Lua pattern special characters).

params.name: pattern
params.description: Lua pattern (or literal text when plain=true).

params.name: init
params.description: 1-based start index (negative counts from the end). Default 1.

params.name: plain
params.description: When true, disables pattern matching and does a plain substring search.

returns.description: start, end [, captures...] on match; nil on no match

examples.code:
local S, E = string.find('hello world', 'wor')
print(S, E)  -- 7  9

local S2, E2, Cap = string.find('MRN:12345', '(%d+)')
print(Cap)   -- "12345"

items.name: string.format
items.description: Returns a formatted version of its variable number of arguments following the description given in formatstring, which follows the rules of the C `printf`.

examples.code: print(string.format('%s = %05d', 'count', 42))  -- "count = 00042"

items.name: string.gmatch
items.usage: for cap1, cap2 in string.gmatch(s, pattern) do ... end
items.description: Returns an iterator function that, each time it is called, returns the next captures from pattern over string s. If pattern has no captures, the whole match is returned each time.

returns.description: iterator function, for use in a generic for loop

examples.code:
for word in string.gmatch('one two three', '%a+') do
   print(word)
end
-- one
-- two
-- three

items.name: string.gsub
items.description: Returns a copy of s in which all (or, if n is given, at most n) occurrences of pattern have been replaced by repl. repl may be a string (with %1..%9 capture references and %0 for the whole match), a table (indexed by the first capture), or a function (called with the captures; its result replaces the match, or the match is kept unchanged if it returns nil/false).

params.name: repl
params.description: Replacement string, capture-indexed table, or replacement function.

params.name: n
params.description: Maximum number of substitutions; default is unlimited.

examples.code:
local Out, N = string.gsub('hello world', 'o', '0')
print(Out, N)  -- "hell0 w0rld"  2

local Wire = ('ADT^A01|20260101'):gsub('%^', '-')
print(Wire)    -- "ADT-A01|20260101"

local Redacted = string.gsub('SSN: 123-45-6789', '%d', '#')
print(Redacted)  -- "SSN: ###-##-####"

items.name: string.len
items.description: Receives a string and returns its length. Equivalent to the `#` operator on a string.

examples.code:
print(string.len('hello'))  -- 5
print(#'hello')             -- 5

items.name: string.lower
items.description: Receives a string and returns a copy of it with all uppercase letters changed to lowercase; other characters are unchanged.

examples.code: print(string.lower('HELLO'))  -- "hello"

items.name: string.match
items.summary: Return the first match's captures (or the whole match).
items.description: Looks for the first match of pattern in s, starting at position init, and returns the captures from the pattern, or the whole match if the pattern specifies no captures. Returns nil on no match.

params.name: init
params.description: 1-based start index (negative counts from the end). Default 1.

returns.description: captures... (or the whole match); nil on no match

examples.code:
local Mrn = string.match('MRN:12345', 'MRN:(%d+)')
print(Mrn)  -- "12345"

items.name: string.rep
items.description: Returns a string that is the concatenation of n copies of s, optionally separated by sep between each pair.

examples.code:
print(string.rep('ab', 3))       -- "ababab"
print(string.rep('ab', 3, '-'))  -- "ab-ab-ab"

items.name: string.reverse
items.description: Returns a string that is the string s reversed.

examples.code: print(string.reverse('hello'))  -- "olleh"

items.name: string.sub
items.description: Returns the substring of s that starts at i and continues until j; i and j can be negative, counting from the end of the string. The default for j is -1 (the end of the string).

params.name: i
params.description: Start index (1-based, negative counts from the end).

examples.code:
print(string.sub('hello world', 1, 5))  -- "hello"
print(string.sub('hello world', -5))    -- "world"

items.name: string.upper
items.description: Receives a string and returns a copy of it with all lowercase letters changed to uppercase; other characters are unchanged.

examples.code: print(string.upper('hello'))  -- "HELLO"

modules.name: debug
modules.title: Lua Debug Library
modules.description: Standard Lua 5.1 debug library: introspection and instrumentation for the call stack, locals, upvalues, and metatables. debug.traceback is the one function commonly useful in workflow scripts (paired with xpcall to capture where an error occurred); the rest are low-level tools for advanced debugging.

items.name: debug.traceback
items.description: Returns a string with a traceback of the call stack, optionally prefixed with message. Commonly used as the message handler passed to xpcall to capture where an error occurred.

params.name: message
params.description: Text to prefix the traceback with.

params.name: level
params.description: Stack level to start the traceback at. Default 1 (the caller).

examples.code:
local Ok, Err = xpcall(RiskyFn, debug.traceback)
if not Ok then print(Err) end

items.name: debug.getinfo
items.summary: Get information about a function or stack level.
items.description: Returns a table with information about a function, or about the function running at the given stack level. what selects which fields to fill in ("n" name, "S" source, "l" current line, "u" upvalues, "f" the function itself); default is all of them.

params.name: function
params.description: A function value, or a stack level (integer, 0 = current function).

params.name: what
params.description: Field selector string. Default all fields.

returns.description: table of debug info, or nil if the level is out of range

examples.code:
local Info = debug.getinfo(1, 'Sl')
print(Info.source, Info.currentline)

items.name: debug.getlocal
items.summary: Read a local variable of a stack frame.
items.description: Returns the name and value of the local variable at index in the function at stack level level. Returns nil if there is no local at that index.

params.name: level
params.description: Stack level (1 = the caller of debug.getlocal).

returns.description: name, value, or nil if index is out of range

examples.code: local Name, Value = debug.getlocal(1, 1)

items.name: debug.setlocal
items.summary: Write a local variable of a stack frame.
items.description: Sets the value of the local variable at index in the function at stack level level to value. Returns the variable's name, or nil if there is no local at that index.

returns.description: name, or nil if index is out of range

examples.code: debug.setlocal(1, 1, 42)

items.name: debug.getupvalue
items.summary: Read an upvalue of a function.
items.description: Returns the name and value of the upvalue at index of function f. Returns nil if there is no upvalue at that index.

returns.description: name, value, or nil if index is out of range

examples.code: local Name, Value = debug.getupvalue(SomeFn, 1)

items.name: debug.setupvalue
items.summary: Write an upvalue of a function.
items.description: Sets the value of the upvalue at index of function f to value. Returns the upvalue's name, or nil if there is no upvalue at that index.

returns.description: name, or nil if index is out of range

examples.code: debug.setupvalue(SomeFn, 1, 42)

items.name: debug.getmetatable
items.description: Returns the metatable of object, or nil if it has none. Unlike getmetatable(), ignores the __metatable field, so it can inspect protected metatables.

examples.code: local Meta = debug.getmetatable(SomeValue)

items.name: debug.setmetatable
items.description: Sets the metatable for object to table (which can be nil). Returns object. Unlike setmetatable(), ignores the __metatable field.

params.name: table
params.description: New metatable, or nil to remove it.

examples.code: debug.setmetatable(SomeValue, SomeMeta)

items.name: debug.getfenv
items.description: Returns the environment table of object.

examples.code: local Env = debug.getfenv(SomeFn)

items.name: debug.setfenv
items.description: Sets the environment table of object to table. Returns object.

examples.code: debug.setfenv(SomeFn, {})

items.name: debug.gethook
items.description: Returns the current hook function, hook mask, and hook count set with debug.sethook, or nothing if there is no active hook.

examples.code: local Hook, Mask, Count = debug.gethook()

items.name: debug.sethook
items.description: Installs hook as a debug hook, called on the events selected by mask ("c" calls, "r" returns, "l" every line), and optionally every count instructions. Call with no arguments to remove the current hook.

params.name: hook
params.description: Hook function, called as hook(event, line).

params.name: count
params.description: Also call the hook every count instructions.

examples.code:
debug.sethook(function(event, line) print(event, line) end, 'l')
-- ... 
debug.sethook()  -- remove the hook

items.name: debug.getregistry
items.description: Returns the registry table, a predefined table used by C code to store Lua values.

examples.code: local Registry = debug.getregistry()

items.name: debug.debug
items.description: Enters an interactive mode, reading and running Lua commands from stdin until the user types "cont". Not useful in Linkiir workflow scripts, which have no interactive stdin — documented for stdlib completeness only.

examples.code:
-- Not useful outside an interactive Lua REPL.
-- debug.debug()
